reasons: The backend start command names main:app, which may not match the file reviewed in this project.
The frontend uses a development server command rather than a production build.
Ollama requires an NVIDIA GPU, which is not checked or explained in the file.
A placeholder password appears in the commented PostgreSQL block. It is not active, but it should be replaced if the block is turned on.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Frontend, backend, and Ollama services
sections.what: Describes three programs to run together: the web screen on port 3000, the Python backend on port 8001, and the Ollama language model server, which needs a graphics card.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets one command start every part of the app with the right connections already set.
sections.watch_out: The backend start command loads a module named main, but the backend code reviewed here is named app_backend.py. Confirm the backend folder has a main.py before starting.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Redis and optional PostgreSQL database
sections.what: Starts a Redis service that saves its data to disk, and declares the storage volumes that keep data between restarts. A PostgreSQL database setup is kept in comments so it can be switched on.
sections.why: Likely reason: Redis is set up as a task queue for background work, and PostgreSQL is an option for a larger database. The comments say the PostgreSQL block is optional.
sections.watch_out: The commented PostgreSQL block contains a simple password. If someone turns it on, they should replace it first. The backend also lists Redis as a startup requirement, although the code reviewed here does not show it being used.

summary: Starts the frontend web screen, the Python backend, the Ollama language model server and Redis together as containers.
purpose: Lets one command start the whole app stack with the connections between parts already set.
why: Likely reason: avoids setting up each program by hand and keeps the ports and addresses in one place.
how: 1. Builds the frontend from the frontend folder and runs its development server on port 3000. 2. Builds the backend from the backend folder, stores data in the data folder, connects it to Ollama and Redis, and runs it on port 8000 inside the container, shown on port 8001. 3. Runs Ollama with access to an NVIDIA graphics card and keeps downloaded models in a volume. 4. Runs Redis with saved data. 5. Keeps a PostgreSQL database setup in comments, ready to switch on.
inputs: The Dockerfile in the frontend folder, the Dockerfile in the backend folder, the environment settings listed in this file, and the data folder.
outputs: Four running services on ports 3000, 8001, 11434 and 6379, plus stored data in the volumes.
risks: The backend command loads a module named main, but the backend code reviewed here is named app_backend.py. The frontend runs a development server, which is not meant for live use. Ollama needs an NVIDIA GPU or it will not start. Ports are opened to the machine network.
debug: Run the compose logs command for the service that fails. For the backend, confirm the backend folder has a main.py file. For Ollama, confirm the NVIDIA driver and container toolkit are installed. Check that ports 3000, 8001, 11434 and 6379 are not already in use.
